## AI/Semiconductor Catalyst Monitor — 2026-07-05

### Fresh Developments (last 24-72h)

**Signal 1 — DRAM/HBM Pricing**
TrendForce Q3 2026 print (July 3): conventional DRAM **+13–18% QoQ**, NAND +10–15% QoQ. Memflation decelerating sharply from Q1 (+93–98%) and Q2 (~+60%) but **no reversal** — AI/server demand is the floor; consumer affordability ceiling is the brake. Separately, a US antitrust suit (17 plaintiffs vs. Samsung/SK Hynix/Micron, filed ~June 25-29, widely covered July 2-3) alleges coordinated production cuts engineered ~700% DRAM price rise over 4 years; not a pricing catalyst but a headline risk for all three stocks. MU initially -4% on memory supply-glut fears (Samsung/SK Hynix capacity adds) then bounced +9.9% in Monday recovery.

**Signal 2 — HBM4 Ramp / Correction Risk**
SK Hynix **intentionally delayed HBM4 line conversions** in favor of DDR5 (margins ~90% in 2026). Full-year 2026 HBM4 shipment revised down to ~4B Gb. Samsung counter-moved: HBM4 cumulative revenue crossed **$1B** in 4 months. 2027 HBM contract negotiations **stalled** — suppliers pushing for 'multiples higher'; TrendForce June 2 report still the live thesis. SK Hynix's diversion tightens HBM4 supply into H2 2026 — bears against the "correction after 2026" scenario.

**Signal 3 — Hyperscaler AI Capex — No Guide-Down, But Watch Q2 Earnings**
**NVIDIA Vera Rubin first shipments confirmed rolling NOW in July** to AWS, Google, Microsoft, OCI, CoreWeave, Lambda, Nebius, Nscale. Mass production ramps Q3, broad availability Q4. Jensen Huang cited $1T in Blackwell + Vera Rubin orders through 2027 at GTC. NVDA Q1 FY2027 revenue $81.6B; Q2 guide **$91B ±2%** (well above $86.84B consensus). **No hyperscaler has guide-down**: Amazon ~$200B, Microsoft ~$190B, Alphabet ~$180-190B (raised), Meta ~$125-145B (raised from $115-135B). Total 2026 hyperscaler capex ~$695-725B. **Watch:** Q2 earnings late-July — analysts flagging this as earliest possible first guide-down window.

**Signal 3 — Breaking: Meta Compute (July 1)**
Bloomberg broke: Meta is launching a **cloud business to sell excess AI compute** — undercutting AWS/Azure by 20-30% using MTIA custom silicon. Three-tier offering: raw GPU compute, hosted Llama models, AI agent platform. Potential launch as early as July 2026. Meta stock +9% on the news; CoreWeave -13-15%, Nebius -15%, IREN sharply lower. SoftBank followed July 2 with **SB Neo**, a new neocloud targeting 10 GW by 2030. Together these signal structural pressure on pure-play GPU rental neoclouds. Meta MTIA v3 in production mid-2026.

**Signal 4 — AMD/ASICs**
No AMD MI400/Helios GA announcement. **Next catalyst: AMD Advancing AI 2026 event July 22-23** (Moscone Center) — Lisa Su keynote July 23 expected to confirm Helios GA timeline, MI455X/MI450 availability, MI500 roadmap. AMD Q1 2026 data center rev $5.8B (+57% YoY), Q2 guide $11.2B. Oracle confirmed first Helios deployment: 50,000 MI450 GPUs in Q3. Meta committed to Helios for H2 2026. Google TPU Ironwood (v7) at scale; v8 (Sunfish/Zebrafish, TSMC 2nm) targets late 2027. Marvell projecting up to $11B AI ASIC revenue for 2026.

**Signal 5 — Optical/Photonics**
A **CPO rollout delay report** hit the optical group hard: AAOI -17%, COHR -10%, LITE -10%. Raymond James raised COHR PT $371 → $435 (Strong Buy, July 2) despite the pullback. Stifel raised PTs on COHR/LITE/CIEN ahead of earnings. COHR also signed LOI for up to $50M in CHIPS Act funding. InP lead times unchanged at 52–58 weeks. CRDO separately announced **DustPhotonics acquisition** (~$1.3B total) for Silicon Photonics PIC capabilities targeting $500M+ optical revenue FY2027 — closing expected Q2 2026. CIEN: No fresh 72h news.

**Signal 6 — Solar**
**July 4 ITC safe harbor deadline just passed** under the "One Big Beautiful Bill" (OBBBA signed July 4, 2025) — projects that did not begin construction by July 4 face drastically tighter timelines (placed-in-service by Dec 31, 2027). This is a hard policy cliff; near-term uncertainty on how much pipeline was successfully locked in. FSLR hit by **multiple securities class action filings July 1-4** alleging the company overstated ability to manage tariff impacts and understated facility underutilization (class period Feb 2025 - Feb 2026). ARRY -6.1%, NXT -5.5% in solar flush. ENPH + SolarEdge each +8% on June 30 on AI datacenter power/OCP theme, then pulled back. Guggenheim raised FSLR PT $215 → $225 (July 2, Buy). UFLPA tightening (12 new Chinese suppliers added July 3) and IRA domestic content adder reaffirmed June 30 are modestly constructive for FSLR long-term.

---

### Context (vs. Baseline)

- Memflation decel (+13–18% Q3) is on-baseline trajectory; cycle is cooling from extremes, not reversing.
- SK Hynix diverting HBM lines to DDR5 **tightens** H2-2026 HBM4 supply — directly undercuts the baseline "correction after 2026" bear case.
- Hyperscaler capex not only intact but tracking ~$695-725B total (above $600-700B baseline); Meta and Google both raised.
- AVGO's soft Q3 AI guide ($16B vs $17.2B) is the near-term sentiment overhang — not a demand destruction signal but a pace-of-acceleration signal.
- Meta Compute entering cloud is a **structural wildcard** — could reshape how AI compute supply/demand is priced (meta builds for itself and now sells excess; neoclouds pressured).
- NVDA Vera Rubin shipping now is a direct demand validation — this is the real-time check on the $350B+ NVDA revenue bull case (baseline cited ~$350B; current FY2027 consensus appears ~$245-270B, suggesting baseline may be FY2028 bull case or high-end scenario).
- FSLR class action + ITC cliff are fresh solar bears not in the baseline.

### Most Important Development

**NVIDIA Vera Rubin first shipments confirmed physically rolling to hyperscalers in July** is the single most structurally significant event of the week — it validates the continued AI infrastructure buildout at maximum scale with next-gen hardware. Paired with Meta's entry into cloud compute (undercutting rivals 20-30%), the week's two dominant narratives are: (1) AI hardware demand is accelerating, not plateauing, and (2) the compute supply chain is becoming vertically integrated at hyperscalers in ways that reshape economics for everyone below them. AVGO's soft guide is the near-term sentiment overhang to watch heading into late-July Q2 earnings season, where any hyperscaler capex guide-down would be the first real bear catalyst for this cycle.
